clue.text: Explosive man of Kent?

definitions.meaning: a high explosive based on picric acid, first tested at a range in Kent
playfully, a native of Lydd, a town on Romney Marsh in Kent, by the pattern of words like Israelite

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered Kentishman is described.
explanation.walkthrough: Lydd is a small town in the English county of Kent; the explosive was named after the firing range there, and the clue's question mark lets it double as a name for a local man.
explanation.definitionFit: The picric-acid shell filling took its name from the Kent town where it was proved.

clue.text: Down-to-earth striker

parts.note: something that strikes the ground from the sky, not a practical industrial worker or footballer

explanation.surface: A practical, unpretentious footballer or industrial striker.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt from a storm strikes down to the ground, literally striking earth.

clue.text: Coercive cavalryman ?

parts.note: a mounted soldier whose name is also a verb meaning to force someone into doing something

explanation.surface: A bullying horse soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted infantryman; and as a verb, to bully or force into compliance.

clue.text: Gave as an example what Denis can't remedy

indicators.note: to remedy is to put right, here by putting the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Denis is unable to fix something that was cited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what' joins; 'remedy' rearranges DENIS CAN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite a case is to mention it as an illustration.

clue.text: Observe entry in rules Pythagoras made

indicators.note: the answer enters into the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Note something going into rules Pythagoras devised.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of is to notice or see.

clue.text: Wave washing up wildly?

definitions.meaning: a large wave that curls and crashes on the shore
jokingly, someone who smashes the crockery while doing the dishes carelessly

explanation.surface: A wave washes ashore, or someone does the dishes clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaker is a sea wave that crashes; also one who smashes things, as a careless dishwasher does.

clue.text: Precious reluctant group donor ?

parts.note: you can't get blood out of a stone, so the most unwilling blood donor is a stone; precious makes it a gem

explanation.surface: A precious person is reluctant to give blood of a certain group.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'you can't get blood out of a stone' makes a stone the least willing donor; 'Precious' says it is a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A green chalcedony spotted with red, a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Time for the GI to stir himself!

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An American soldier is told it is time to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir himself' reads as getting up; 'stir' rearranges THE GI.
explanation.definitionFit: A time on the clock, as in 'meet at eight'.

clue.text: Ape-king captures a member in Malay village

indicators.note: the ape king holds the other pieces inside him

parts.note: King Kong, the giant ape of the film
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A giant ape seizes someone in a village.
explanation.definitionFit: A kampong is a small settlement or hamlet in Malaysia.

clue.text: Fairy-cycles on the 9?

parts.note: the circles of darker growth on a lawn are called fairy ...; cycles are circles

explanation.surface: Bicycles for fairies ride on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the lawn plant at 9 across; fairy circles appear on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy rings are circles of mushrooms on lawns; cycles here are circles.

clue.text: Not the growing understanding of an opportunist

definitions.text: Not the growing understanding of an opportunist

parts.words: Not the growing understanding of an opportunist
parts.note: 'Not the growing under-standing' plays on that phrase

explanation.surface: Someone who seizes chances is slow to grasp things.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'understanding' into 'under-standing': the opportunist does not let the stuff grow under where he stands, the idiom for wasting no time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'not let the lawn-stuff grow under one's feet' means acting promptly, as an opportunist does; the missing word is the plant.

clue.text: Gray, plodding type who flunked the exam?

definitions.meaning: Thomas Gray's Elegy has the farm worker who 'homeward plods his weary way'
'plough' is old British university slang for failing an examination, so one ploughed is a failure

explanation.surface: A grey, dull plodder who failed the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gray' is the poet Thomas Gray, not the colour; his Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard opens with this figure plodding home.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's Elegy pictures a farm labourer plodding home; and to be ploughed was old Oxbridge slang for failing an exam.

clue.text: A great success in river traffic to and fro

indicators.note: the success is placed inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
a wow is a sensational hit

explanation.surface: A big hit in river traffic going both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' joins the parts: the definition describes traffic moving in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement in both directions is the defining feature of a road or street with opposite lanes.

clue.text: Whereby Fleet Street noised it all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters of the words are jumbled

explanation.surface: The national press spread a story widely.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was the London home of Britain's national newspapers; 'all over the place' rearranges NOISED IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers publish through successive printed issues, the means by which the press spreads news.

clue.text: Spring came madly with a rush

indicators.note: acting madly, the letters run about into a new order

explanation.surface: Spring arrived suddenly and in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season or the definition, but it is fodder: 'madly' rearranges SPRING CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Running hurriedly is moving with haste, as a child darts about.

clue.text: Greek style of electricity charge ?

definitions.meaning: a classical order of architecture with scroll capitals
relating to charged atoms, as in a bond between oppositely charged particles

explanation.surface: A question about Greek design and an electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical architectural orders; also an adjective for charged particles in chemistry.

clue.text: Ay, in the — ye go for men" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: Ay, in the — ye go for men" (Macbeth)

parts.words: Ay, in the — ye go for men" (Macbeth)
parts.note: Macbeth tells the murderers they pass as men in the list of mankind, as hounds and curs all pass as dogs

explanation.surface: A quotation from Macbeth with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: Macbeth, Act 3, says the murderers count as men only in the general list, as all breeds count as dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means a list or register, the inventory in which all men are counted alike.

clue.text: A sucker for Scotch on the rocks!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: whisky is a liquor
on the rocks means served with ice

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled into liking whisky with ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sucker' is not a dupe but a sweet to suck; 'on' puts LIQUOR above ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The black sweet is something sucked, like a lollipop.

clue.text: An issue for the country after European Monetary Agreement

indicators.note: the country follows behind the abbreviation

parts.note: M stands for Monetary
A stands for Agreement
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A national matter following a European currency deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that flows or issues forth from a source is an outpouring.

clue.text: Soldiers who could be armed with guns

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: Troops who might carry weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins ARMED and GUNS, the letters 'could be' reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a regiment of Guards are soldiers, such as those outside Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Article not on her but someone else

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a person who isn't her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A different person, a second one besides the first.

clue.text: Name price of, say, a share

indicators.note: spoken, the word runs on into the following a with its final letter silent

parts.note: to quote is to state the price of

explanation.surface: Give the price of a share, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'quote a' runs together as one word meaning a fixed portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A quota is a fixed portion or allocation, a share allotted to each.

clue.text: Open-air theatre company's "'Ishmael "?

parts.note: out means outdoors, in the open air
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: An outdoor theatre company stages Ishmael.
explanation.walkthrough: Ishmael, son of Abraham in Genesis, was sent away into the desert, so the name stands for a rejected person.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Ishmael was banished, the type of the rejected exile.

clue.text: Joint not to be given cold to one's friends

definitions.meaning: a cut of meat or a body joint at the top of the arm

definitions.text: not to be given cold to one's friends
definitions.meaning: to 'give someone the cold' this is to snub them, which one should not do to friends

explanation.surface: A cut of meat that should not be served cold to friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball-and-socket joint at the arm; and the idiom 'cold' this means to ignore someone deliberately.

clue.text: Sort of hat shows up 28's cheeky blemishes

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: the wild pig at 28 has growths on its face

explanation.surface: A hat reveals spots on someone's cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater or panama is woven from dried stalks, a type of summer hat.

clue.text: Not how dieters should show amusement

definitions.text: Not how dieters should show amusement

parts.words: Not how dieters should show amusement
parts.note: the proverb says to do this 'and grow fat', so slimmers should avoid it

explanation.surface: Advice that slimmers shouldn't express joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The old saying 'Laugh and grow fat' is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing amusement by chuckling, which the proverb says fattens.

clue.text: Alias Balthazar, Daniel II

definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice the heroine disguises herself as a young lawyer called Balthazar
Gratiano hails her in the trial as 'a second Daniel', the wise judge of the Bible

explanation.surface: A list of aliases for a man named Daniel.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves refer to Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice: the disguise in court, and the praise 'A Daniel come to judgment... a second Daniel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's heiress takes the lawyer's name Balthazar and is praised as a second wise judge Daniel.

clue.text: Proverbs lacked publicity for a long time

indicators.note: the proverbs go without the publicity

parts.note: adages are sayings or proverbs
ad is short for advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: Proverbs were not advertised for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacked' removes AD from ADAGES, leaving AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is informal for a very long period.

clue.text: Poor Hero availing herself of provision of fresh quarters

indicators.note: in poor shape, so the letters of the name are jumbled

parts.note: to avail oneself of something is to use it

explanation.surface: An unfortunate woman takes advantage of new accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for Hero, but it is the anagram signal for her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving people into new homes is giving them fresh accommodation.

clue.text: Bad air, first question for a Baghdad type

indicators.note: bad here marks the letters of the word as spoiled and jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: Foul air raises a question for someone from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' signals the anagram; 'first' gives I as the Roman numeral one, which goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital of Iraq, so a person from there is a native of that country.

clue.text: A growth destroyed by a wild animal

indicators.note: a thing destroyed is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tumour is eaten away by some creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The African wild pig with facial bumps is a wild animal.

clue.text: Tiny component in gun to make it more pleasing

indicators.note: the tiny part is set inside the gun

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun of World War II
wee is Scottish for tiny

explanation.surface: A small part fitted to a gun improves it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'component' simply joins: the tiny piece goes in the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To add sugar or charm is to render something more agreeable.
